excerpt.rendered: “I am willing. Be cleansed.” Four words to a leper. “Ephphatha.” One word to a deaf man’s ears. Jesus often healed with the shortest sentences in the New Testament.

content.rendered:
“I am willing. Be cleansed.” Four words to a leper. “Ephphatha.” One word to a deaf man’s ears. Jesus often healed with the shortest sentences in the New Testament. The brevity itself preached a sermon about the authority behind the words.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, October 11, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 9

Today’s Scripture

“Then Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out His hand and touched him, and said to him, ‘I am willing; be cleansed.’ As soon as He had spoken, immediately the leprosy left him, and he was cleansed.”
Mark 1:41-42 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

A leper approached Jesus one day in Galilee and knelt before Him with a request that was almost shocking in its courage. “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” In the ancient world, leprosy was a death sentence. The leper was required by law to live outside the camp, to tear his clothes, to cover his upper lip, and to cry out “Unclean! Unclean!” wherever he went to warn healthy people to stay away. He had not been touched by a human hand in years. Jesus, moved with compassion, did the two things that defied every social convention of the day. He stretched out His hand and touched the leper. And He spoke four of the shortest, most authoritative words in the entire New Testament. “I am willing. Be cleansed.” Mark tells us that as soon as He had spoken, immediately the leprosy left the man, and he was cleansed.

This pattern recurs throughout Jesus’ healing ministry. He often did not give lengthy prayers. He gave short, direct, authoritative commands to the body or the condition. To a deaf man in Mark 7, He looked up to heaven, sighed, and said one Aramaic word. “Ephphatha.” Which Mark translates for his Greek readers, “Be opened.” The man’s ears were immediately opened. To a man with a withered hand in Mark 3, Jesus said, “Stretch out your hand.” The hand, which the man could not stretch out, stretched out and was restored. To a man by the Pool of Bethesda in John 5 who had been sick thirty-eight years, Jesus said, “Rise, take up your bed and walk.” Immediately the man was made well. Over and over, the pattern is the same. A short, authoritative word. Instant obedience from the body or the condition.

The Passion Translation captures the warmth and the authority: “Jesus, deeply moved with tender compassion, reached out and touched him, and said, ‘Of course I am willing to heal you, and now you will be healed!’ Instantly his leprosy disappeared—his flesh became smooth and healthy!” (Mark 1:41-42 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds the completeness of the result: “And immediately the leprosy [completely] left him and he was made clean [by being healed]” (Mark 1:42 AMPC). Completely. The authority of the command produced a complete result.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Short. Direct. Addressed to the condition itself. Four words to leprosy. One word to deaf ears. The format matters. The believer is not required to pray eloquently or lengthily to see healing. The believer is required to speak with authority, from faith, in the name of Jesus.

The Essence. Jesus did not negotiate with the sickness. He did not plead with the sickness. He commanded the sickness, and the sickness obeyed. The spiritual principle is that sickness, in the Kingdom economy, is subordinate to the authority of Christ. When that authority is exercised through the believer, the sickness is still subordinate.

The Authority. Jesus delegated this exact authority to His disciples when He sent them out. “He called the twelve to Himself, and began to send them out two by two, and gave them power over unclean spirits” (Mark 6:7). And later: “These signs will follow those who believe: In My name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new tongues; they will take up serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it will by no means hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover” (Mark 16:17-18). The authority is not reserved for apostles. It is given to those who believe.

The Assurance. “I am willing.” This is the critical phrase. The leper had asked if Jesus was willing. Jesus settled the question in one sentence. The Father’s will on healing is not uncertain. The cross settled it. Isaiah 53:5 declares, “By His stripes we are healed.” The believer who prays for healing is not pleading with a reluctant God. The believer is enforcing a settled covenant.

The Submission. The believer’s authority is always exercised in the name of Jesus, not in the believer’s own name. The believer does not heal. The believer speaks the word that Jesus has authorised, and Jesus heals through the believer’s words. The glory belongs to Him.

The Result. Immediate. Complete. Visible. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, do not be afraid to pray short, direct, authoritative prayers over sickness. Yours or someone else’s. “In the name of Jesus, be healed.” “In the name of Jesus, be opened.” “In the name of Jesus, be whole.” The brevity is not the issue. The authority is. And the authority has already been given to you.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Father, I thank You that healing is settled in the finished work of Christ. By His stripes I am healed. The Father’s will is not uncertain. The covenant is already paid for.

Command. In the name of Jesus, I speak to [name the sickness, the pain, the condition — in yourself or in the person you are praying for]. Be cleansed. Be opened. Be made whole. Leave this body now. The Father has already said yes.

Faith Declaration. I believe the healing is already released. I thank the Father in advance for the manifestation that is on its way.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Healing is settled in Christ. By His stripes I am healed. My short, authoritative prayers in the name of Jesus carry the full authority of the One who commanded leprosy to leave and deaf ears to open. I speak healing today.
